judged_text: The constructor now unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token to refresh tokens on every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService, replacing jsforce's on-demand refresh-on-401 behavior, and overwrites the stored credential key on every call. Every Salesforce calendar operation (including reads with a valid unexpired access token) makes an extra network round-trip to Salesforce, and concurrent calls race to overwrite the credential row; if Salesforce rate-limits or the refresh fails, previously-working calendar access now fails.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an `await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` refresh flow unconditionally before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, and then immediately updates the credential row via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This means every instantiation triggers an extra network call and can fail calendar operations if the refresh request is rate-limited/errored even when an existing access token might still be usable. The unconditional write also introduces a race when multiple instances run concurrently, repeatedly overwriting the same credential row.
